questionText:
Read the following excerpt on Kshitindranath Majumdar's masterpiece 'Rasa-Lila' and answer the questions that follow:

Painted in 1926 by Kshitindranath Majumdar, 'Rasa-Lila' is one of the most spiritually radiant and lyrical achievements of the Bengal School wash tradition. Majumdar, who was revered as a 'Bhakta-Shilpi' (Saint-Artist) for his lifelong devotional immersion in the Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Vaishnava faith, translates the mystical Maha-Rasa of Vrindavana into a celestial visual reverie. In the painting, Lord Krishna dances in a harmonious ring with the cowherd maidens (Gopis) in a sacred grove under the silvery glow of the full moon. Majumdar's figures are distinguished by their extraordinary elongated grace, slender willow-like waists, and sinuous undulating lines that sway with musical cadence. The flowering branches of Kadamba trees drape over the dancers, framing the ecstatic circular dance against translucent, pastel washes of pale mauve, soft saffron, and dusky blue, conserved in the National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi.

Statement I: Jamini Roy deliberately rejected his formal British academic training and Bengal wash style to embrace the raw, earthy folk idiom of Bengal village patuas.

questionText:
Read the following excerpt on the statutory Flag Code, proportions, and symbolism of the National Flag and answer the questions:

The National Flag of India is a horizontal tricolour of three equal rectangular panels: India Saffron (Kesari) at the top, White in the middle, and India Green at the bottom. The ratio of the width (height) to the length of the flag is strictly 2 : 3. In the center of the white band is the Ashoka Chakra, rendered in navy blue, containing 24 equally spaced spokes. As explained by Dr. S. Radhakrishnan in the Constituent Assembly, Saffron denotes renunciation, courage, and dedication to service; White denotes the path of light, truth, purity, and non-violence; and Green denotes our connection to the soil, plant life, and material prosperity upon which all life depends. The Ashoka Chakra, adapted from the 3rd-century B.C. Sarnath Lion Capital of Emperor Ashoka, represents the eternal Wheel of the Law (Dharma Chakra), dynamic motion, and the peaceful progress of the nation, while its 24 spokes symbolize round-the-clock advancement and foundational ethical virtues.
